original_value: Recently, various technologies for utilizing unmanned aerial vehicles have been studied. Drones are a kind of unmanned aerial vehicle. Drone-based mobile surveillance systems can be applied for various purposes such as object recognition or object tracking. In this paper, we propose a mobility-aware dynamic computation offloading scheme, which can be used for tracking and recognizing a moving object on the drone. The purpose of the proposed scheme is to reduce the time required for recognizing and tracking a moving target object. Reducing recognition and tracking time is a very important issue because it is a very time critical job. Our dynamic computation offloading scheme considers both the dwell time of the moving target object and the network failure rate to estimate the response time accurately. Based on the simulation results, our dynamic computation offloading scheme can reduce the response time required for tracking the moving target object efficiently.

result.paraphrase: Recently, many technologies for using unmanned aerial vehicles have been studied. Drones are a type of unmanned aerial vehicle. Drone-based mobile surveillance systems can be used for a variety of tasks, including object recognition and object tracking. In this paper, we propose a mobility-aware dynamic computation offloading scheme that can be applied to tracking and recognizing a moving object on the drone. The proposed scheme aims to shorten the time needed to recognize and track a moving target object. This reduction is important because recognition and tracking are highly time-critical tasks. Our dynamic computation offloading scheme estimates response time accurately by taking into account both the dwell time of the moving target object and the network failure rate. Simulation results show that the scheme can efficiently reduce the response time needed to track the moving target object.
